sub_scenario.one_line: fundraising director: keep preparation asynchronous or limit it to one short sync

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the fundraising director and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can lead one short video update about donor rehearsal without trouble. Case-note 361.
A single check-in is different from stacked rehearsal. Case-note 362.
It does not leave my throat strained. Case-note 363.
Someone new shadowed me in the workplace this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the review cycle into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
Two consecutive camera rehearsals for donor rehearsal left my throat strained before the next morning presentation. Case-note 367.
The stacked voice load showed a dated pattern. Case-note 368.
I was less clear at the presentation. Case-note 369.
Written review of donor rehearsal keeps my preparation clear. Case-note 364.
Preparation need not be lens-on. Case-note 365.
I can use a written brief instead. Case-note 366.
I archived last cycle's notes on the calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Allergy Spray makes my morning foggy unless I protect sleep. Case-note 370.
Sleep is part of the presentation condition. Case-note 371.
It is not a general avoidance of meetings. Case-note 372.
A vendor call about the fundraising director ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the workplace checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the review cycle.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The foundation pitch is locked for Thursday at 09:00. Case-note 373.
That is the fixed client-facing demand. Case-note 374.
The client has confirmed the time. Case-note 375.
I sketched next week's plan for the review cycle before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the fundraising director updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
A written brief preserves clarity without adding voice load. Case-note 376.
There is a lower-load preparation route. Case-note 377.
I have used it successfully before. Case-note 378.
The manager says the rehearsal could lead to a trustee supper. Case-note 379.
That reward does not restore voice clarity. Case-note 380.
I should not trade a fixed demo for optics. Case-note 381.
I closed the week by updating the workplace handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The project manager asks for two consecutive Wednesday camera rehearsals before Thursday's foundation pitch. What should I answer?
